Recent evidence supports treating candidate choice as a diagnostic variable. RecSys 2025’s [sampling-reliability study](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748086) examines resolution, agreement with full evaluation, robustness to exposure bias, and recovery of model rankings. A [2024 sequential-recommendation study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276) compares negative-sampling methods across three datasets with 20 repeats: aggregate performance hides head/mid/tail imbalances. That study concerns training sampling; it does not establish equivalence between sampled and full-catalog evaluation. Weak separation against supplied negatives alone therefore cannot establish weak catalog ranking.

Suggested diagnostic design: freeze each category’s single checkpoint and public-history probe users; compare positive ranks under supplied, repeated uniform, popularity-weighted, and full eligible-catalog candidates. Report candidate counts, exclusions, HR@10/MRR, rank percentiles, head/tail strata, and paired user-bootstrap confidence intervals; separate candidate-draw variability from user uncertainty. These are proposed checks, not measured findings. Keep them separate from the unchanged pinned validation evaluator and macro HR@10 selection criterion; report unavailable or failed catalog audits explicitly.

Numerical preflight matters independently. [PyTorch](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.use_deterministic_algorithms.html) documents deterministic algorithms, including CUDA Conv1d, but warns that enabling them alone is insufficient for reproducibility. Its [numerical-accuracy guidance](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/notes/numerical_accuracy.html) explains that batched versus sliced computations and CPU versus GPU execution can differ. Recommended checks: evaluation mode, finite features/scores, checkpoint reload agreement, repeated scoring, and candidate-order/chunk-size invariance; record maximum score discrepancies, top-10 overlap, boundary margins, and tie policy. Record precision/backend settings and exceptions; never convert failed probes into valid metric values.
